name: Felix Dzerzhinsky
summary: A Polish nobleman's son who spent much of the two decades before 1917 in tsarist prisons and exile, and who from 20 December 1917 ran the All-Russian Extraordinary Commission - the Cheka - which is the institution the civil war left behind it. Ascetic, incorruptible and entirely without doubt, he is the reason the argument about the terror is an argument about a state organ rather than about a mob.
